findings.title: Evaluating Synthetic Sentence Coherence Using a Large Language Model
findings.key_contribution: Uses SUMO's ~20,000 concepts and 100,000 higher-order logic statements to generate millions of synthetic sentences with formal representations, then uses LLMs to filter for linguistic coherence to improve training data quality and ontology common-sense rules.
findings.relevance: Demonstrates SUMO as a large-scale formal ontology grounding for LLM training data generation and validation, directly relevant to Autognosia's neuro-symbolic memory where ontology provides structured reasoning substrate.

findings.title: Embedding Deontic Logic Operators from a Large Ontology in Higher-order Logic
findings.key_contribution: Translates SUMO's deontic axioms (modal logic) into TPTP Typed Higher-order Form (THF) for automated theorem proving with Vampire, enabling quantification over formulas in a 20K constant / 100K formula ontology.
findings.relevance: Shows SUMO's expressive power for deontic/normative reasoning in higher-order logic — useful for Autognosia's memory architecture where obligations, permissions, and institutional facts need formal representation.

findings.title: Language to Logic Training Corpus and Sigma Updates
findings.key_contribution: New language-to-logic translation project with publications; KIF and TPTP file editor in Sigma; TPTP tests for calendar and modal reasoning; Neo4j exports of SUMO graph content.
findings.relevance: Direct tooling improvements for SUMO-to-logic translation and graph export — enables Autognosia to leverage SUMO as a formal backbone with modern graph database integration and LLM-friendly translation pipelines.

findings.title: ISO/IEC 21838-2:2021 Basic Formal Ontology (BFO) - Standard Status 2026
findings.key_contribution: BFO-2020 standardized as ISO/IEC 21838-2:2021 — the only top-level ontology with ISO standardization. 35 classes, ~45 relations, OWL 2 and Common Logic axiomatizations. US DoD/IC adopted BFO + Common Core Ontologies as baseline standard (2024).
findings.relevance: BFO's ISO standardization and DoD/IC adoption make it the de facto standard for interoperable ontology engineering. Autognosia should align its upper-level categories (continuant/occurrent, independent/dependent) with BFO for maximum interoperability.

findings.title: BFO-2020 GitHub Repository and Artifacts
findings.key_contribution: Maintains BFO-core.owl, OWL 2 implementations (RDF/XML, Functional, Turtle), Common Logic (CLIF), Prover9, and SPARQL quality checks. BFO-CCO Office Hours for community support.
findings.relevance: Provides machine-ready, version-controlled BFO artifacts with quality assurance — Autognosia can directly import BFO-core.owl as its upper ontology foundation with confidence in logical consistency.

findings.title: From Human Intuition to Causal Graphs: A DOLCE-Based Human-Ensembled Neuro-Symbolic Architecture
findings.key_contribution: Uses DOLCE's endurant/perdurant distinction to map Kahneman's System 1 (intuition as endurant selection) and System 2 (reasoning as perdurant inference). Binds via Vector Symbolic Architectures into unified causal graphs grounded in cognitive categories.
findings.relevance: Directly applicable to Autognosia: DOLCE's cognitive ontology provides the formal bridge between intuitive/associative memory (System 1) and deliberate/symbolic reasoning (System 2) — exactly the dual-process architecture Autognosia's memory system needs.

findings.title: Digital Twins as Information Artefacts: A DOLCE-Based Foundational Account
findings.authors: CAOS Workshop / JOWO Episode XI / FOIS 2025
findings.key_contribution: Formalizes Digital Twins as DOLCE-based information artefacts with 'differential qualities' — stakeholder-goal-shaped qualities with causal relevance for diagnostics, optimization, simulation.
findings.relevance: DOLCE's artefact/function theory applied to digital twins — relevant for Autognosia's memory as a 'cognitive digital twin' of the agent's knowledge state, with goal-directed differential qualities for memory consolidation.

findings.title: Approximating DOLCE in OWL: DOLCEbasic and DOLCEnaryRel Core Modules
findings.key_contribution: OWL approximations of DOLCE (DOLCEbasic, DOLCEnaryRel) with consistency proofs via MACE4/Prover9. Makes DOLCE usable in standard Semantic Web toolchains.
findings.relevance: Enables Autognosia to use DOLCE's cognitive distinctions (endurant/perdurant, quality/role) in OWL-based knowledge graphs with automated reasoning support.

findings.title: GOLEM Ontology for Narrative and Fiction Extending DOLCE
findings.key_contribution: GOLEM extends CIDOC CRM + LRMoo + DOLCE's cognitive foundations for narrative/fictional elements, enabling provenance tracking and pluralistic interpretations.
findings.relevance: Shows DOLCE as cognitive foundation for complex representational domains (narrative, fiction) — supports Autognosia's need to represent hypothetical, counterfactual, and narrative memory traces.

findings.title: ONTrust: A Reference Ontology of Trust via DOLCE
findings.key_contribution: Reference ontology of trust built on DOLCE for AI/blockchain trust conceptualization, supporting automated reasoning and semantic interoperability.
findings.relevance: DOLCE-based trust ontology relevant for Autognosia's memory provenance, source reliability tracking, and multi-agent epistemic trust modeling.

findings.title: A Methodological Framework for Runtime Ontology Evolution in Dynamic Environments
findings.key_contribution: Proposes methodological/architectural approach for runtime updating of ontologies and KBs to support decision-making in dynamic, partially known environments.
findings.relevance: Directly addresses Autognosia's need for ontology evolution at runtime as the agent encounters new domains, contradictions, and concept drift.

findings.title: The Co-evolution of Ontologies and Extensive Knowledge Graphs on a Web Scale
findings.key_contribution: Engineering framework for construction, validation, and evolution of vast, real-time, reliable knowledge graphs with ontology co-evolution.
findings.relevance: Web-scale co-evolution patterns applicable to Autognosia's memory-as-knowledge-graph that must evolve continuously with agent experience.

findings.title: Active Ontology: The 2026 Default for Enterprise AI
findings.key_contribution: Active ontology = machine-readable model bound to live metadata, lineage, governance. Static ontologies drift by day 30. Four co-located graphs (data, governance, knowledge, active ontology) share metadata lakehouse. Agents query via MCP at inference time.
findings.relevance: Paradigm shift from static to active ontology — Autognosia's memory architecture should adopt active ontology principles: continuous binding to live experience, lineage tracking, and inference-time querying via MCP.

findings.title: Evo-DKD: Dual-Knowledge Decoding for Autonomous Ontology Evolution
findings.key_contribution: Embeds validation within decoding loop, autonomously updating ontologies in real-time without human intervention while maintaining structured coherence through internal gating.
findings.relevance: Fully autonomous ontology evolution with internal validation — a target architecture for Autognosia's self-evolving memory where the agent validates its own conceptual changes.

findings.title: Ontology-Grounded Project Memory for Coding Agents (MOOSEDev)
findings.key_contribution: MOOSEDev gives coding agents structured, ontology-grounded project memory via knowledge graph exposed through MCP. Records carry lifecycle status, provenance, supersession links. Uses neurosymbolic engine (MOOSE) treating symbolic layer as primary reasoning substrate.
findings.relevance: Direct blueprint for Autognosia: ontology-grounded memory with lifecycle, provenance, supersession — exactly the structured memory architecture Autognosia needs for persistent, auditable agent memory.

findings.title: Toward Effective and Reliable LLM Agents via Dynamic Ontology (OaK)
findings.key_contribution: OaK framework dynamically constructs task-oriented ontologies for LLM agents: constructs ontology + KG from task data, generates task-adaptation functions for graph reasoning, refines with judge feedback. Ontology as active kernel mediating LLM-task environment.
findings.relevance: Dynamic, task-conditioned ontology construction — Autognosia can adopt OaK's approach of building fit-for-purpose ontologies per task/context rather than one monolithic ontology.

findings.title: Automatic Ontology Construction Using LLMs as External Memory, Verification, and Planning Layer
findings.key_contribution: Neuro-symbolic architecture: LLM as interpretation/generation/orchestration layer over external ontological graph (RDF/OWL) + vector RAG + SHACL + SPARQL + dialogue logs. Enables long-term memory, explainability, contradiction control, robust planning.
findings.relevance: Complete architecture matching Autognosia's vision: LLM + ontology graph + validation + query + logs as integrated memory system. The 'external memory layer' pattern is directly applicable.

findings.title: Blending Ontologies and Language Models for Robot Explanations
findings.key_contribution: Ontology-based reasoning + LLM for sound, natural robot explanations. Episodic memory → ontology-guided retrieval → narrative construction → explanation generation.
findings.relevance: Episodic memory indexed by ontology for explanation generation — relevant for Autognosia's memory retrieval and explanation/self-reporting capabilities.

findings.title: Knowledge Cards: Structured Knowledge for AI Systems
findings.key_contribution: Knowledge Cards: ontology-grounded, provenance-linked, boundary-explicit, expert-validated, versioned structured knowledge units for agentic AI decisions. Gartner 2026 calls semantic layer foundational for enterprise AI.
findings.relevance: Knowledge Card pattern for Autognosia's memory units: each memory trace as a validated, versioned, provenance-tracked knowledge card grounded in ontology.

findings.title: Memory as Ontology: Constitutional Memory Architecture for Persistent Digital Citizens (Animesis)
findings.key_contribution: Reconceives memory as the agent's existence itself (not a function). 'Constitution Layer' = immutable memory rules. Retrieval as cognitive (not performance) operation. Designed for persistent identity across model upgrades.
findings.relevance: Radical reframing: memory = identity/constitution. Autognosia should adopt constitutional memory principles — certain core memories immutable, retrieval as cognitive process, persistent identity across sessions.

findings.title: WorldDB: Vector Graph-of-Worlds Memory Engine with Ontology-Aware Write-Time Reconciliation
findings.key_contribution: Memory engine with recursive 'worlds' (nodes as containers with subgraphs, ontology scopes, composed embeddings). Edit propagation invariant ensures structural isolation. Ontology-aware reconciliation at write time. Beats Mem0, Supermemory, Zep on LongMemEval.
findings.relevance: Recursive world/scoped memory with ontology-aware write reconciliation — directly applicable to Autognosia's multi-context memory (episodic, semantic, procedural worlds with isolation).

findings.title: Nested Episodic State Topology (NEST): Graph-Theoretic Architecture of Cognitive States
findings.key_contribution: NEST = foundational graph-theoretic representational ontology for cognition as structured state formation/transformation. Typed weighted graphs with subgraph payloads. Six relation classes: causal, containment, temporal, associative, evidential, spatial. Separates durable belief graphs from working-memory graphs. Maps ACT-R, Soar, Sigma, Common Model, Global Workspace Theory as constrained regions.
findings.relevance: Major advance: a unified cognitive ontology (NEST) that formalizes memory, belief, working memory, self, and maps major cognitive architectures. Autognosia can use NEST as its cognitive ontology foundation — more comprehensive than HiTOP for AI agent cognition.

findings.title: Examining Foundational Assumptions of HiTOP (Philosophical Case Conference)
findings.venue_date: Philosophy, Psychiatry, & Psychology Vol 33 No 2, June 2026
findings.key_contribution: Structured philosophical examination of HiTOP's assumptions: dimensionality, hierarchy, latent variables, psychopathology concept, validity, epistemic/non-epistemic values. Commentaries address hierarchy justification, latent variables as causal mechanisms, dimensionality vs pluralism.
findings.relevance: Shows HiTOP's limitations for AI: agnostic on causation, descriptive not mechanistic, focused on psychopathology not general cognition. Autognosia needs a cognitive ontology with causal/mechanistic commitments (like NEST).

findings.title: Do Cognitive Functions Belong in HiTOP? Meta-Analysis
findings.key_contribution: Meta-analytic joint factor analysis integrating 8 DSM disorders + 7 cognitive functions. Finds general factor loading on all, three superspectra: psychosis+cognitive dysfunction, externalizing, emotional dysfunction. Shows cognitive abilities integrable into HiTOP.
findings.relevance: Demonstrates HiTOP expanding to include cognitive functions — but still psychopathology-focused. Autognosia needs a cognitive ontology for *normal* cognition (memory, reasoning, planning) not psychopathology.

findings.title: Rebuilding HiTOP from Ground Up: Symptom-Level Analyses
findings.key_contribution: Deconstructs DSM disorders into symptoms, rebuilds HiTOP from ground up (n=11,762). Finds similar structure but with broad hypomania/disinhibition and pathological introversion as prominent differences.
findings.relevance: Methodological advance in bottom-up ontology construction from data — relevant for Autognosia's data-driven ontology learning from agent experience.

findings.title: Epistemic Limits and Ontological Primitives: Sāṃkhya and Hoffman on Consciousness
findings.key_contribution: Critiques Hoffman's Conscious Realism/Conscious Agent Theory for relying on unexplained functional primitives (perception, decision, action). Proposes Sāṃkhya dualism (Puruṣa = pure witness consciousness, Prakṣti = matter) as ontological framework resolving the tension.
findings.relevance: Cross-traditional ontology of consciousness primitives — relevant for Autognosia if modeling artificial consciousness/self-awareness: need ontological primitives for 'witness' vs 'content' in memory architecture.

findings.title: The Science of Consciousness 2026 Conference (TSC 2026)
findings.key_contribution: Major conference with 14 plenary sessions: quantum biology, neuroscience, AI, psi, origins of consciousness. Topics: quantum AI & consciousness, cerebral organoids, anesthesia, 'Is AI Conscious?' panel, non-local consciousness.
findings.relevance: Tracks latest consciousness science relevant to Autognosia's potential self-modeling / metacognitive memory — especially quantum AI, cerebral organoids, and AI consciousness sessions.

findings.title: Neuroscience of Consciousness Volume 2026 Issue 1
findings.key_contribution: Special issues: 'Aware & Alive: Embodied and Phenomenological Perspectives', 'Spontaneous Thought and Consciousness', 'Computational Approaches to Neurophenomenology'. Papers on connectivity-based NCCs, vivid imagery timing, tACS, hypnotic consciousness, dream/wake bridging, meditation/predictive processing, DMT micro-phenomenology, brain organoid ethics.
findings.relevance: Cutting-edge empirical consciousness research with computational/neurophenomenological approaches — Autognosia's memory architecture could incorporate neurophenomenological memory models (e.g., meditation-trained attention, dream/wake state transitions).

findings.title: Emergent, Dynamic Ontology Generation in Neurocognitive Memory Systems
findings.key_contribution: Deployed system where ontology *emerges* from neurocognitively structured memory substrate, evolves with corpus, and is *observed by the system itself* with provenance-grounded, access-controlled record of conceptual change. Inspired by Tulving/Squire multi-system memory neuroscience.
findings.relevance: Direct match for Autognosia: self-observing, provenance-tracked, neurocognitively-grounded ontology evolution. The 'system observes its own conceptual change' is a key Autognosia requirement.

findings.title: Active Ontology: The 2026 Default for Enterprise AI
findings.key_contribution: Active ontology stays bound to live metadata, lineage, policy. Four co-located graphs. Agents query via MCP at inference time. Static ontologies drift by day 30.
findings.relevance: Active ontology = self-evolving by definition. Autognosia should implement active ontology pattern with MCP inference-time querying.

findings.title: Σ0–EvoCell: AI-Native Ontology Unifying Evolutionary and Cell Biology in Latent Space
findings.key_contribution: Evolutionary Cell Ontology (ECO) on Σ0 substrate: 16 structural operators as knowledge glyphs, tensor ops, and dual semantics (evolutionary + cellular timescales). Same operator = speciation (phylogenetic) = APC/C commitment (cell-cycle). AI-native formal language.
findings.relevance: AI-native ontology with operators carrying dual semantics across timescales — inspiring for Autognosia's memory operators that must work across episodic (fast) and semantic (slow) timescales.

findings.title: Knowledge Graph Re-engineering Along the Ontological Continuum
findings.key_contribution: Ontological continuum framework: semantics vs pragmatics, properties vs affordances. Characterizes, compares, navigates, transforms KGs across modeling practices. Five open challenges for neuro-symbolic AI KG adaptation.
findings.relevance: Framework for evolving KGs across ontological commitments — Autognosia can use this to migrate its memory KG across ontology versions/frames as the agent's understanding evolves.

findings.title: OntoLearner: Modular Python Library for Ontology Learning with LLMs
findings.authors: Babaei Giglou, D'Souza, Aioanei, Mihindukulasooriya, Auer
findings.key_contribution: 180 machine-readable ontologies across 22 domains, pipeline-ready datasets with train/dev/test splits for 3 core OL tasks (term typing, taxonomy discovery, non-taxonomic relation extraction). Large-scale empirical study: 22 retrieval models × 12 LLMs. Finding: failure modes scale with *ontological complexity*, not model size. Primary bottleneck = structural mismatch between model encodings and ontology organization.
findings.relevance: Standardized benchmark infrastructure for ontology learning — Autognosia can use OntoLearner to evaluate its own ontology induction from agent experience. Key insight: complexity mismatch is the real challenge.

findings.title: SCOPE and SCION: Benchmark and Auditable Pipeline for Schema Induction from Text
findings.key_contribution: SCOPE = train-text-only benchmark for corpus-to-schema induction + optional schema fusion from 24 IE sources normalized to gold schema graphs. SCION = auditable pipeline with contract-constrained LLM modules, evidence pointers, conservative alignment to base ontology with provenance.
findings.relevance: Benchmark for schema induction from raw text with auditable provenance — directly applicable to Autognosia's ontology learning from agent dialogue/experience logs.

findings.title: When Does Bigger Help? Controlled Study of LLM Scale for Ontology Learning
findings.key_contribution: Controlled evaluation of 13 models (Qwen3.5/3.6 dense/MoE, GPT variants) on OntoLearner pipeline across 4 biomedical/materials ontologies. Non-taxonomic relation extraction remains hard. Architecture/lineage outweighs parameter count. Model size alone insufficient for OL.
findings.relevance: Empirical guidance for Autognosia's LLM selection for ontology learning tasks: prioritize architecture/domain adaptation over raw scale.

findings.title: FAIR Compliance, AI-Readiness, and Ontology Maturity of Garment Datasets
findings.key_contribution: Systematic assessment of 64 fashion datasets on FAIR compliance, AI-Readiness Score, 5-level ontology maturity model. 79.7% only flat annotations (Level 2 or below). Shows maturity model for ontology evaluation.
findings.relevance: 5-level ontology maturity model as evaluation framework — Autognosia can assess its own memory ontology maturity level.

findings.title: DaoQL: Explicit World Model with Counterfactual Reasoning Evaluation
findings.key_contribution: Data-first ontology: LLM as reasoning engine, deterministic knowledge in explicit multimodal DB (DaoQL). Formalizes explicit world model with counterfactual decomposability. 34/34 query coverage, 94% composable counterfactual decomposability vs 45% for GPT-4o alone. LDBC/ANN benchmarks.
findings.relevance: Benchmark for explicit world models with counterfactual reasoning — Autognosia's memory should support counterfactual queries (what-if reasoning) as a key evaluation metric.

findings.title: MetaHarmonizer: Biomedical Metadata Harmonization with Contamination Control
findings.key_contribution: Contamination-controlled evaluation protocol showing LLM accuracies on public benchmarks substantially inflated (memorization). OntologyMapper achieves 77.9-95.5% Top-1 on EFO benchmarks. Calibrated confidence scores (AUC 0.73-0.94) for human-in-the-loop triage.
findings.relevance: Critical methodology: contamination-controlled benchmarks for ontology tasks. Autognosia must evaluate its memory/ontology learning on held-out, contamination-controlled test sets.

findings.title: NeuSymMS: Hybrid Neuro-Symbolic Memory System for Persistent, Self-Curating LLM Agents
findings.key_contribution: NeuSymMS: neural fact extraction (LLM) + CLIPS expert system for classification, deduplication, reconciliation under explicit lifecycle rules. Knowledge as subject-relation-value triples in RDBMS. Dual-horizon (short/long-term) memory. Access-based promotion, time-based pruning. Three-tier scoping (user/agent/agent-to-agent). Zero-cost, low-latency deterministic decisions with rule-based justifications.
findings.relevance: Production-ready neuro-symbolic memory architecture with expert system (CLIPS) for deterministic lifecycle management — directly implementable pattern for Autognosia's memory layer.

findings.title: Advancing Multimodal Agent Reasoning with Long-Term Neuro-Symbolic Memory (NS-Mem)
findings.key_contribution: NS-Mem: three-layer memory (episodic, semantic, logic rule layer). SK-Gen automatically consolidates structured knowledge from multimodal experience into symbolic DAGs with neural indices. Hybrid retrieval: similarity search + deterministic symbolic query. 4.35% avg reasoning improvement, 12.5% on constrained reasoning. Incremental updates via EMA + structural DAG modifications.
findings.relevance: Three-layer neuro-symbolic memory with procedural DAGs in logic layer — excellent match for Autognosia's episodic/semantic/procedural memory distinction. SK-Gen for automatic consolidation from experience.

findings.title: Aeon: High-Performance Neuro-Symbolic Memory Management for Long-Horizon LLM Agents
findings.key_contribution: Aeon = Cognitive OS: Memory Palace (Atlas: SIMD-accelerated page-clustered vector index with small-world graph navigation + B+ tree disk locality) + Trace (neuro-symbolic episodic DAG with typed edges: CAUSAL, NEXT, REFERS_TO). Semantic Lookaside Buffer (SLB) predictive caching for sub-ms retrieval. Zero-copy C++/Python bridge via nanobind. 85%+ SLB hit rate.
findings.relevance: High-performance systems-level neuro-symbolic memory: spatial index (Atlas) + episodic DAG (Trace) + predictive cache (SLB). Autognosia can adopt the Cognitive OS metaphor: memory as managed OS resource with allocation/paging/context-switch.

findings.title: Mimir: Neuro-Symbolic Memory with Dynamic Grounding for Embodied Agents
findings.key_contribution: Separates world memory (object locations, states, perceptual evidence) from task memory (goal agenda, progress, hand state, failures, constraints). Dynamic grounding binds active goal to recalled world evidence before each action. 42.5% max / 23% avg gains on EB-ALFRED/Habitat. 86% success on long-horizon EB-Habitat with open-source 32B model beating closed-source.
findings.relevance: World/Task memory separation with dynamic grounding — directly applicable to Autognosia: world memory = semantic/episodic knowledge, task memory = current goal stack, grounding = retrieval conditioned on active goal.

findings.title: Aligning Progress and Feasibility: Neuro-Symbolic Dual Memory Framework
findings.key_contribution: Dual memory: neural Progress Memory (stage-aware semantic blueprints from successful trajectories) + symbolic Feasibility Memory (executable Python verifiers from failed transitions). Unified inference loop: Progress proposes, Feasibility verifies/refines. Beats baselines on ALFWorld, WebShop, TextCraft. Reduces invalid actions and trajectory length.
findings.relevance: Progress/Feasibility dual memory maps to Autognosia's prospective/retrospective memory or System 1/System 2 — neural for semantic guidance, symbolic for constraint verification.

findings.title: Hybrid Self-Evolving Structured Memory for Computer-Use Agents (HyMEM)
findings.key_contribution: HyMEM: graph-based memory coupling discrete symbolic nodes + continuous trajectory embeddings. Self-evolution via node add/merge/replace. On-the-fly working memory refresh detecting phase shifts (VLM compares transitions). +22.5% on Qwen2.5-VL-7B, surpasses GPT-4o/Gemini. Multi-hop seed-and-expand retrieval.
findings.relevance: Self-evolving hybrid graph memory with on-the-fly refresh — closest to Autognosia's vision: discrete+continuous, graph-structured, self-evolving, phase-aware working memory refresh.

findings.title: Synapse: Episodic-Semantic Memory via Spreading Activation
findings.key_contribution: Synapse: dynamic graph memory with spreading activation (not pre-computed links). Lateral inhibition + temporal decay. Triple Hybrid Retrieval: geometric embeddings + activation-based graph traversal. Beats SOTA on LoCoMo for temporal/multi-hop reasoning. Solves 'Contextual Tunneling'.
findings.relevance: Spreading activation over dynamic graph — biologically plausible retrieval for Autognosia. Solves the 'contextual tunneling' problem (over-focusing on recent/retrieved context).

findings.title: Neuro-Symbolic Meta-Policies for Temporal Knowledge-Graph Memory under Partial Observability
findings.key_contribution: Meta-policy learns which symbolic memory heuristic to apply (QA, exploration, forgetting) on temporal RDF knowledge-graph memory (RoomKG). Qualifier-aware StarE-GNN encoder. Preserves step-level traceability. Beats symbolic and neural baselines at memory capacity 512.
findings.relevance: Learned meta-policy over symbolic memory operations — Autognosia can learn *how to manage its own memory* (what to retrieve, consolidate, forget) while keeping operations symbolic and inspectable.
